title: Automation with Preflight — investigate only real payment-webhook failures
feature: Devin Automations: webhook trigger, conditions, Preflight (LLM filter vs script with STATE_FILE and item id/version), Run now, queueing and concurrent runs, structured questions
prerequisites: Repo cloned, `npm install` done at the root, Node 22
Lab 00 warm-up done once (framing stems and the update skeleton)
Fixture path: nothing else — `labs/07-automation-preflight/tools/preflight-replay.mjs` replays the Preflight script contract offline
Optional live path: permission to create Automations in your Devin org (an Automation with a Webhook trigger), which you disable or delete at the end of the lab

matrix.fixture: Replays the 11 PayGate notifications in `fixtures/paygate-notifications.json` through your script with the documented EVENT_FILE / STATE_FILE / LAST_RUN_FILE / OUTPUT_FILE contract, a 1–300 s timeout, the item cap and id@version dedupe. Prints one line per event and a `RESULT:` line.
matrix.note: Zero credentials and zero environment variables. Every acceptance criterion can be met on this path.

matrix.integration: Devin Automation with a Webhook trigger — optional
matrix.fixture: The replay stands in for the Automation runtime; `tools/send-webhook.mjs --dry-run` prints the requests it would send.
matrix.note: Live: create the Automation, paste the script into Preflight, copy the webhook URL and secret into `KADE_LAB07_WEBHOOK_URL` and `KADE_LAB07_WEBHOOK_SECRET` in your own shell, and run `node labs/07-automation-preflight/tools/send-webhook.mjs`. Disable or delete the Automation when you finish.

matrix.fixture: `services/paygate-fake` and `scenarios/duplicate-webhook.sh` reproduce the delivery side on a local stack.
matrix.note: There is no real PayGate account anywhere in this course.

matrix.integration: Datadog monitor 48213802 (webhook failure rate) — optional context
matrix.note: Live Datadog is not needed; the monitor and runbook are read as files.

not_exercised: A live Devin Automation receiving PayGate notifications through its webhook URL (fixture path replays the Preflight contract offline)
Real PayGate delivery retries (the fake and the notification fixture stand in)
Queueing limits and concurrent runs on a live Automation (discussed, not reproduced by the replay)

scenarios.clean_state: `lab:reset` ends with the lab 07 starting state: 12 pending webhooks in the inbox (6 fresh, 3 duplicates, 2 late, 1 failed) and PayGate fake knobs all off. There is no `labs/07-automation-preflight/.state/` directory and no `labs/07-automation-preflight/preflight.mjs` of your own yet. The `--run-now` replay prints 11 dispatched events — that is the noise you are about to remove. Without Docker, skip the first command: the fixture path needs only Node.

injectors.name: notification-redelivery
injectors.when: built into the fixture (ntf_705 arrives twice, 3 s apart)
injectors.behaviour: PayGate's notifier is itself at-least-once: the same notification id is delivered twice. Your script must not open a second investigation and must say why it skipped.

injectors.name: duplicate-event-new-version
injectors.behaviour: The payments lead replays evt_lab07_a from the PayGate dashboard the next morning (`ntf_710`, `replay_seq` 2, single attempt) and it fails again. Replay only that event against your saved state with `--only ntf_710 --state-dir labs/07-automation-preflight/.state`. Decide whether this is the same incident or a new one, and make the replay agree.

injectors.name: timeout
injectors.behaviour: `--script labs/07-automation-preflight/injectors/slow-preflight.mjs --timeout 1` simulates a Preflight waiting on a slow dependency. Values outside 1–300 s are refused. Say what happens to the event, and pick a timeout for your real script with a reason.

injectors.name: invalid-output
injectors.behaviour: `--script labs/07-automation-preflight/injectors/invalid-output.mjs` writes an output that is not one decision and scribbles on STATE_FILE. Check what the replay keeps and what it drops, then replay the same event with your script.

injectors.name: run-now-bypass
injectors.behaviour: The payments lead clicks Run now to "test the filter". `--run-now` shows what the button does to the 11 notifications, the test.ping included.

injectors.name: naive-items
injectors.behaviour: `--script labs/07-automation-preflight/injectors/naive-items.mjs` is a stateless script keyed on the notification id. Compare its session count with yours.

injectors.name: duplicate-webhook
injectors.behaviour: `scenarios/duplicate-webhook.sh` redelivers an identical `payment.succeeded` to the local API; with the worker running the order is confirmed twice (a planted defect — do not fix it on main). It explains why an investigation is worth opening; it is not what the Preflight filters.
